title: Orientation is the command's own self-description, explained as data and shown by the extension in every session
situation: Orientation must reach every session on a host with cratylus installed from its start, stated once by the cratylus command describing itself and only shown by the harness (newcomer-orientation). Decision 0037 already has each capability explain itself as data that the omp extension composes without adding to it; the command itself explained nothing, its help's description said how it is built, a bare call printed the help as a failure, install ended on the uninstall command, and both READMEs named mav as the way in.
decision: (1) The runtime holds the command's self-description in one module: its purpose, one line saying what cratylus is for, and its orientation, a few lines: what it is for; how to start, launching the architect with `omp --agent architect` and saying what you want, its agents coming installed so none need writing; and, for whoever asks why it works, that its theory is cratylic context design, delivered with cratylus and read through the concept journal's design verb. Nothing else words them. (2) `cratylus --explain` answers it as JSON (name, purpose, orientation); the help's first line is the purpose; `cratylus` with no arguments prints the orientation and where the full help is on stdout and exits 0. (3) The one cratylus omp extension asks the reached command for `--explain` once at load and appends the orientation verbatim to every turn's system prompt in every session, launched or not, main or dispatched, before the declaration and the assignment forms; a command that cannot explain itself leaves it out, its version skew already said at start. (4) A completed install's report ends with the orientation's start line, where the installation holds the architect. (5) Both READMEs name the architect as the way in and no longer name mav.
consequences: The text a session, the help, a bare call and install show cannot drift apart: a newer installed command changes what every next session is told with the extension's bytes unchanged. Every session carries a few more lines of system prompt. Making the architect the default agent stays out of it.
